114.label: PR #114
114.title: Primary straight-line AGM and runtime bounds

description: The logical route from the deployed verifier to the formal soundness endpoint.

stages.title: Pin Lean to the deployed verifier
stages.claim: The Lean assembler and a captured Rust verifier MSM agree coefficient-for-coefficient on the checked fixture.
stages.summary: The proof starts by fixing the object under study: the verifier's final multi-scalar multiplication. MsmMatch transfers a checked coefficient match to equality of group evaluations, but the deployed evidence remains fixture-based rather than a universal Rust-to-Lean equivalence.
proves: The checked Lean and captured Rust MSM coefficients match.
A matching MSM has the same group evaluation under any supplied URS.
residuals: Rust capture provenance and opaque-tag to Vesta-point faithfulness.
Deriving the deployed verifying key and circuit description inside Lean.

stages.title: Turn acceptance into the IPA equation
stages.claim: An accepting assembled MSM yields halo2's explicit IPA verifier equation.
stages.summary: DeployedAccepts is the concrete MSM-equals-identity premise. deployedAccepts_verifierEq unfolds that compact check into the equation consumed by the soundness argument while retaining the verifier's rejection guards.
proves: The compact deployed accept implies the explicit verifier equation.
The soundness development now reasons about the equation actually assembled by the verifier.
residuals: The empirical verifier-fingerprint boundary from the preceding stage.
Fiat-Shamir challenges still need an oracle/rewinding interpretation.

stages.title: Rewind the oracle and assemble a tree
stages.claim: Enough accepting reprogrammed runs produce three distinct nonzero accepting continuations at every IPA round.
stages.summary: Transcript-ordering lemmas seal each round prefix before its challenge. The verifier equation becomes a concrete prover-strategy predicate, the counting forking lemma produces the branching executions, and deployed_forking_tree assembles them into the transcript tree used by special soundness.
proves: Round messages precede the challenges they must not influence.
The probability threshold yields the full accepting tree required by extraction.
residuals: Blake2b and challenge decoding are idealized as a uniform random oracle.
This #24 tree theorem is a consumer; the computed adversary, query-loss, and certificate producer are composed in the AGM stage.

stages.title: Peel the auxiliary generators
stages.claim: The deployed tree reduces to either a clean g-only IPA tree or a nontrivial relation over (g, U, W).
stages.summary: The deployed equation carries the U and W terms used for values and blinding. deployed_to_acceptV removes them when z is nonzero. Failure to separate them is exposed explicitly as the relation branch rather than hidden behind a binding axiom.
proves: The auxiliary-generator terms are removed on the clean branch.
Binding failure is retained as an explicit relation on the deployed augmented basis.
residuals: The legacy propositional capstones retain z != 0 and other rung-specific structural premises.
The relation branch needs a computational reduction, not a propositional impossibility claim.

stages.title: Extract the IPA opening
stages.claim: A clean ternary transcript tree determines one witness that opens the commitment at the claimed inner product.
stages.summary: ipa_soundV applies three-special-soundness recursively. Distinct nonzero challenges make the Vandermonde reconstruction invertible, producing one coefficient vector shared by the commitment and value equations.
proves: The extracted vector commits to the verifier's pinned commitment.
The same vector has the extracted inner product value.
residuals: ipa_soundV consumes a completed tree; the deployed FS path constructs that tree in the AGM stage.
The alternative relation branch remains computationally meaningful.

stages.title: Price the relation branch
stages.claim: The algebraic Fiat-Shamir game produces PR #28's deployed instances, states binding as a computable value mismatch against the carried aggregate opening (never as nonexistence of an opening, which holds vacuously in a prime-order group), and feeds every mismatch run's explicit relation to the plain-DL probability bound.
stages.summary: PR #28 defines AlgebraicDForkCert and the deployed AGM instance. The programmed-basis relation-to-DL reduction plants the challenge in every basis slot and loses only one 1/|F| hyperplane. PR #56 supplies the executable adaptive side: every adversary-emitted group point carries a basis representation; recursiveAlgebraicFork computes the fork tree from an oracle table and finite tape; algebraicForkCertAttempt_valid proves the resulting certificate valid; and computedDeployedAlgebraicInstance packages it for PR #28. The primary straight-line AGM finder is assembled from the representation-carrying online prover and its staged root, IPA, and constraint-x traces; it has a pointwise four-invocation bound and prices each IPA discrepancy as a pinned quadratic without AFK truncation. The recursive deployed finder remains a separately priced alternative using the unconditional AFK (Attema-Fehr-Klooß-style) expectation, a fixed call budget, and an explicit truncation tail.
proves: Every group point in the adaptive Fiat-Shamir adversary's proof output carries its representation over (g,U,W).
The recursive extractor computes an AlgebraicDForkCert from explicit oracle and tape coins, and every returned certificate records real accepting runs.
Every computed certificate is valid for PR #28's deployed instance, with no Classical.choice at the producer boundary.

On a real binding run - acceptance while the accepted value disagrees with the carried aggregate opening - every produced instance yields an explicit relation: the kernel's relation branch, or the commitment collision between its clean opening and the carried opening.
The full real binding probability is bounded by extraction loss, the z = 0 slice, and the programmed-basis DL term.
The programmed-basis relation-to-discrete-log transformation is deterministic and its miss refers to the same relation; the miss costs exactly one 1/|F| hyperplane.

The recursive extractor has the unconditional field-independent Attema-Fehr-Klooß-style expected-call bound (8·Q+1)·10^k, with no FamilyForkSpread premise. 10^k is large: at the deployed k = 11 and Q = 2^122 the expectation is about 2^161.5, far beyond Vesta's ~2^126 discrete-log cost, so this is a structural polynomial bound rather than a concrete security margin - the concrete margin is the straight-line endpoint's.
The deployed combined finder adds at most three black-box calls, truncates at the fixed budget L, and charges the tail ((8·Q+1)·10^k+3)/(L+1).
For distinct parameter queries, the recursive Fiat-Shamir binding event in the uniform generator-RO model is bounded by the fixed-call discrete-log advantage plus the explicit truncation tail.

The additive straight-line AGM endpoint derives each IPA pinned-root invariant from a staged representation trace and covers accepting failure by the zero slice, 2k IPA roots, deployed multiopen roots, the constraint-x root, or one explicit DLOG relation.
The straight-line combined finder uses at most four prover invocations, so its DLOG capstone has no AFK expectation, truncation, or Markov term.

The direct profile separately accounts for reduction group work and both possible direct-coordinate decodes. At the consensus maximum and T=2^123, oracle work and the profiled complete group-work allowance are each at most 2^126, the two direct decodes share at most 2^123 modeled field/data operations, and the non-DLOG statistical terms are below 2^-84. The reduction group-work allowance remains an explicit profile premise. Thus Pr[failure] <= Adv_DLOG(2^126,2^126) + 2^-84. This is a DLOG-conditional 123-bit protocol work-factor target, not an unconditional failure-probability exponent.

Both the recursive and straight-line runtime endpoints pass through the four-budget semantic promotion, so row-level gate, permutation, and lookup semantics carry explicit y, beta, gamma, and theta prices on top of the compressed identity.

The direct-coordinate postprocessing has a proved field-independent polynomial total-cost model over the exact represented source consumed by the finder: at most numPointSets+1 columns, each traversing at most queryBudget members. At the captured shape it is linear in the action count, and the primary finite-security profile carries its pointwise bound rather than accepting a free reduction-work number.
residuals: Identify deployed Blake2b and halo2's concrete hash-to-curve with their modeled random oracles; supply finite-security Vesta DL hardness and external bounds on the prover and reduction group work; construct the executable root, IPA, and constraint-x stages packaged by ComputedStraightLineDeployedFSFamily.ofCovered; and compose the primary straight-line failure event through the Action terminal with concrete y, beta, gamma, and theta budgets. The captured endpoint reuses existing fixture metadata, while the zero-column captured-data family remains only an interface test.

stages.title: Recover the verifier's opened columns
stages.claim: Rewinding x4 recovers the point-set aggregates; rewinding x1 binds those aggregates to the queried member commitments.
stages.summary: The x4 rewind floor produces a transfer from the pinned IPA opening to the power-batched openings consumed by the Vandermonde decode. The x1 layer then exposes the individual advice, instance, fixed, permutation, lookup, and vanishing commitments inside each aggregate.
proves: The x4 decode yields the deployed point-set aggregates, not modeled stand-ins.
The x1 unbatch pins the extracted witness to the actual queried member commitments.
residuals: The x4 accept-measure premise and an accepting current run remain explicit.
Per-point claimed evaluations and x-to-x3 quotient transport remain in hquot.

stages.title: Lift the point check to circuit satisfaction
stages.claim: Outside the Schwartz-Zippel bad set, the quotient point check implies the full combined gate identity.
stages.summary: The bad-set theorem bounds roots of the constraint-difference polynomial. The xgood capstones spend an accept-measure budget to select a good accepting challenge, removing hgood while keeping the actual quotient-check content in hquot.
proves: A good challenge turns the verifier's point identity into the full gate polynomial identity.
The xgood family derives bad-set avoidance from an explicit probability budget.
residuals: hquot still carries the fingerprint-to-gate-check and x-to-x3 transport content.
Permutation/lookup grand-product telescoping and final lookup assembly are not wired into this relation.

stages.title: Compose legacy opening and circuit satisfaction
stages.claim: The extracted opening and gate identity form SnarkRelation, which the legacy propositional Vesta capstone family exposes at the verifier boundary.
stages.summary: SnarkRelation is the conjunction of one pinned IPA opening and circuit satisfaction for the same witness. The legacy opening and constraint capstones package this route across abstract, deployed, adaptive, rewind, xgood, and x4 variants; the computed explicit-certificate AGM/DL endpoint is tracked separately.
proves: The legacy opening and constraint branches refer to the same pinned verifier statement.
The legacy capstone family makes each modeled adversary and residual hypothesis explicit.
residuals: Different legacy capstones retain different structural and probability premises.
SnarkRelation is not yet the intended high-level Ironwood security statement.

stages.title: Stop at the exact formal boundary
stages.claim: The formal chain reaches SnarkRelation and explicit reduction disjunctions; it does not erase the remaining modeling and composition gaps.
stages.summary: The final view keeps hypotheses and out-of-Lean assumptions visible. This is the honest endpoint: a large mechanized core with named inputs, probability budgets, computational assumptions, and uncomposed execution semantics rather than an all-green claim of end-to-end verification.
proves: Every mechanized bridge shown in the map has a concrete Lean anchor.
The endpoint records reduction outcomes and residual premises without hiding them.
residuals: High-level relation, VK derivation, Rust-capture trust, Blake2b-as-RO, generator hash-to-curve-as-RO, the AGM idealization, and DL hardness.
Runtime extraction, real-adversary execution, oracle-query loss, and combined error budgeting.
